BEFORE THE

JUDY GRACI’S RESPONSE TO APPLICANTS' OBJECTION TO EXHIBITS
Judy Graci (“Ms. Graci”, “Intervenor”), hereby responds to Applicants' objection to her exhibits on the grounds that the exhibits were not produced as part of direct testimony or a discovery response, and respectfully request that the Administrative Law Judges overrule the objection and admit the exhibits into the record.

BACKGROUND
Ms. Graci timely filed direct testimony in this proceeding. Alongside that testimony, Ms. Graci submitted exhibits consisting of publicly available official government and regulatory records, including documents published by the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT), the Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUC), and other sources reflecting current transmission infrastructure and load growth conditions relevant to the issues in this docket. Applicants object to admission of these exhibits solely on the basis that they were not produced in discovery or direct testimony.

ARGUMENT
The Errata and Supplemental Support is Directly Tied to the Direct Testimony
Exhibit 002, Errata and Supplemetal Support to the Direct Testimony of Judy Graci, corrects one factual error identified by Ms. Graci after filing and provides additional evidentiary support for conclusions already stated in Ms. Graci’s Direct Testimony. This Errata does not introduce new issues, new claims, or new legal theories beyond those already presented in Ms. Graci’s Direct Testimony.

Judy Graci’s Requests for Information #3 and #4
These RFI’s are directly tied to the Oncor/LCRA ERCOT load demand submittals for the Permian Basin Reliability Plan.  The Motion to Compel was granted by the ALJ’s.

Official Government and Regulatory Documents Are Not Subject to the Same Foundation Requirements as Private Documents
Exhibits 003 to 008 at issue are not privately created documents requiring discovery production or formal witness sponsorship to establish their reliability. They are official records published by ERCOT and the PUC — the very agencies whose data and findings this Commission routinely relies upon in evaluating transmission necessity and grid reliability. Such records are self-authenticating under applicable evidentiary rules. See Tex. R. Evid. 902(1), (2), (5) (official publications and certified copies of public records are self-authenticating). SOAH proceedings follow the Texas Rules of Evidence as a guide, and the ALJs have broad discretion to admit relevant evidence. 1 Tex. Admin. Code § 155.57.

Requiring Ms. Graci, a pro se Intervenor, to formally sponsor through discovery an ERCOT transmission report or a PUC filing — documents already in the public domain and available to all parties — would elevate form over substance and serve no evidentiary purpose.

The Exhibits Are Directly Relevant to the Issues in This Docket
The Public Utility Commission evaluates Certificate of Convenience and Necessity applications in part based on whether the proposed transmission project is necessary to serve load growth, maintain grid reliability, and meet the needs of the region. See Tex. Util. Code § 37.056. Ms. Graci's exhibits go directly to these issues:

ERCOT’s exhibits are from the PBRP Study, Workshop Groups. and Status Reports, that reflects load forecasting, load breakdown, and load type breakdown — information central to assessing the necessity of the proposed import path projects.
PUC records reflect prior Commission findings and regulatory context applicable to this proceeding.
Permian Basin Off-grid generation lists, current data center and crypto-mining information documents the expansion of large loads in the project region that affects the demand assumptions underlying Applicants' need case, and which Ms. Graci is entitled to place before the ALJs for the Commission's consideration.
Oncor's current transmission project list is Oncor's own data reflecting its existing and pending transmission infrastructure — directly relevant to evaluating whether the proposed project is necessary.

Exclusion of this evidence would deprive the Commission of material information relevant to its statutory findings and would prejudice Judy Graci’s ability to present her case.

CONCLUSION
For the foregoing reasons, Ms. Graci respectfully requests that the Administrative Law Judges:
Overrule Applicants' objection to Ms. Graci’s exhibits;
Admit into the record all exhibits derived from official ERCOT and PUC publications as self-authenticating official government records;
Admit the Permian Basin off-grid generation list, data center information, crypto-mining, and Oncor transmission project list as relevant evidence bearing on the necessity in this proceeding; and
Grant such other relief as the ALJs deem just and appropriate. 

Respectfully submitted,

Bertram, Texas 78605
